demographics.summary: City council now has a 5-2 conservative majority; county commission is 2-1 GOP, shifting oversight of surveillance and policing budgets.
demographics.notes: Council seats remain nonpartisan but functionally align with Republican priorities around surveillance expansions.

demographics.summary: Pueblo city population: 111,456; Pueblo County: 168,424. Median household income (2018-2022 dollars): city $54,137, county $56,567. Poverty rate: city 22.8%, county 18.1%.
demographics.notes: Use these baselines when arguing for equitable deployment of resources and surveillance oversight.

sources: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 2022 5-year subject tables (API)
demographics.notes: Use to illustrate disparities between north-side RTCC corridors (81008) and high-poverty southside ZIP 81005 when debating surveillance budgets.

economy.summary: Rail technology firms, Pueblo Community College, CSU-Pueblo, and downtown tourism funders influence budgets, while surveillance vendors (Daktronics, High Point Networks, Flock Safety) are securing multi-year contracts.
economy.notes: Need quantitative employment data; ties between commissioners and private businesses (Republic Shooting Range, PCC) should be tracked for conflicts.

governance.summary: Pueblo runs a mayor-council government with nine districts; although races are nonpartisan on paper, current alignments track partisan priorities (conservative council bloc, GOP-leaning commission).
governance.notes: Map district boundaries against surveillance deployments and protest corridors to surface representation gaps.

communications.summary: Official website (pueblo.us) posts agendas, news releases, and surveys; Facebook page (facebook.com/CityofPueblo) mirrors alerts and livestreams.
communications.notes: Subscribe to the Agenda Center/newsletter and track Facebook posts for late-breaking policy moves.
